quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Purchasing agents buy the machinery, equipment, tools, parts, supplies or services an establishment needs to operate, including raw or semi-finished materials for manufacturing, and may negotiate contracts.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Purchasing Agents, Except Wholesale, Retail, and Farm Products) include Buyer, Procurement Specialist, Purchasing Agent and Contract Administrator.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a procurement specialist does
paragraphs: Purchasing agents buy the machinery, equipment, tools, parts, supplies or services an establishment needs to operate, including raw or semi-finished materials for manufacturing, and may negotiate contracts.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Purchasing Agents, Except Wholesale, Retail, and Farm Products. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Prepare purchase orders, invite bids and review requests for goods and services.
Analyse price proposals and other data to work out a reasonable price.
Write and review product specifications, keeping a working technical knowledge of what is being bought.
Follow the laws and regulations that apply to purchasing.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BBA (Bachelor of Business Administration); B.Com (Bachelor of Commerce); B.Tech (Bachelor of Technology); Supply Chain Analyst.
Less common routes on the map: Certificate in Stores and Inventory Management.
